units.why: "since the work is not your own" gives the reason for the ban, that AI output is not the student's own work, matching P29.
units.fit_note: Used as the stated reason for a ban, not as a duty.

units.passage: However, achieving these benefits requires the student to use generative AI tools in an appropriate and responsible manner.
units.why: "achieving these benefits requires the student to use generative AI tools in an appropriate and responsible manner" puts responsibility on students: P29.
units.fit_note: Responsibility is about appropriate use, not ownership of submitted work.

units.passage: Affirming your commitment to honor and integrity means affirming that the written work you submit is your own and that you always cite/document anything you did not compose on your own.
units.why: Students should affirm that 'the written work you submit is your own and that you always cite/document anything you did not compose': ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.fit_note: Combines ownership with a duty to cite anything not self-composed.

units.passage: In this course, it is expected that all submitted work is produced by the students themselves, whether individually or collaboratively.
units.why: The Strict statement expects 'all submitted work is produced by the students themselves, whether individually or collaboratively': submitted work must be the student's own, P29.

units.passage: Original Work: While AI can provide assistance, the work submitted by a student must be the student’s own work.
units.why: The text says the work submitted by a student must be the student own work. This is the ownership rule for submitted work, so P29.

units.passage: Students are expected to do all coursework themselves, as an individual or collectively, as designated by the instructor per assignment.
units.why: The closed statement says 'Students are expected to do all coursework themselves'. That is an own-work requirement; P29 (students own what they submit) fits better than P19 since it does not mention generation.
units.fit_note: Own-work expectation within a closed course, with individual or collective work set per assignment.

units.passage: All work submitted in this course must be your own
units.why: Sample (Princeton): "All work submitted in this course must be your own"; students own what they submit, P29.

units.passage: The Composition Program and its teachers assume that work submitted by students–all process work, drafts, low-stakes writing, final versions, and all other submissions–will be generated by the students themselves, working individually or in groups.
units.why: UC Irvine writing-program sample: all submissions "will be generated by the students themselves"; submitted work must be the student's own, P29.

units.passage: In all academic work, the ideas and contributions of others must be appropriately acknowledged and work that is presented as original must be, in fact, original.
units.why: WashU sample: "work that is presented as original must be, in fact, original"; submitted work must be the student's own, P29.

units.passage: takes ultimate responsibility for the content of this publication
units.why: The Bryant sample attribution says the author "takes ultimate responsibility for the content"; students own what they submit, P29.

units.passage: must hold themselves accountable for the decisions and actions taken by the AI systems
units.why: "Faculty, students, and staff must hold themselves accountable for the decisions and actions taken by the AI systems that they choose to use"; ownership, P29.

units.passage: Impress upon your students the fact that if they are putting their name on an assignment, they must take complete responsibility for its content; i.e. if the AI program generates content that does not adhere to the assignment, makes logical errors, or fails to adequately think through a problem, the resulting grade will belong to the student, not the AI program.
units.policy: Instructors impress upon students that if they put their name on an assignment they take complete responsibility for its content, and that the grade belongs to the student, not the AI program, if AI content is flawed.
units.why: 'the resulting grade will belong to the student, not the AI program' says students are responsible for whatever they submit, including AI errors. P29.
units.fit_note: Stresses that AI errors (logical errors, off-assignment content) become the student's grade.

units.passage: However, your final work must reflect your own reasoning and analysis.
units.why: 'your final work must reflect your own reasoning and analysis' requires submitted work to be the student's own thinking, P29.

units.passage: Students are also reminded that they are responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content they submit, regardless of whether they personally authored it or used an AI tool to generate it.
units.why: Students 'are responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content they submit, regardless of whether they personally authored it or used an AI tool', an ownership rule (P29) rather than P31 because it assigns responsibility for submissions.

units.passage: Students are responsible for any content that they produce or publish that includes AI-generated material
units.why: "Students are responsible for any content that they produce or publish that includes AI-generated material" is ownership of submitted work, so P29.

units.passage: AI Use and Student Responsibility Students are responsible for the content produced for the course. Unauthorized AI use can be treated as analogous to assistance from another person or resource.
units.why: "Students are responsible for the content produced for the course" is a general accountability principle for every course product, not tied to a moment of work, so general / must / P29.

units.passage: You are responsible for any content you produce or publish, including AI-generated content.
units.why: "You are responsible for any content you produce or publish, including AI-generated content." The user owns what they publish, P29.

units.passage: You are responsible for ensuring that all submitted content complies with this restriction.
units.why: 'You are responsible for ensuring that all submitted content complies' makes students own compliance, P29.

units.passage: You are responsible for ensuring that all submitted content complies with this restriction. LEVEL 1 Learning Support and Planning You may use generative AI for learning support and planning, such as explaining concepts, generating practice questions, brainstorming ideas, or creating a preliminary outline. You must not include AI-generated language, solutions, analysis, code, media, translations, or revisions in submitted work unless the assignment directions explicitly permit them. You are responsible for ensuring that the central ideas and final work are your own.
units.why: 'You are responsible for ensuring that the central ideas and final work are your own' makes students own their submissions, P29.

units.passage: You will be evaluated on the final product; the quality of your prompts or inputs; accuracy verification, disciplinary judgment, revision, documentation, and reflection; and your ability to distinguish the AI's contributions from your own. You are responsible for the accuracy, quality, and appropriateness of the final work.
units.why: 'You are responsible for the accuracy, quality, and appropriateness of the final work' holds students accountable for the AI-integrated product, P29.

units.passage: Human users have final responsibility for all decisions and outcomes resulting from AI use.
units.why: Accountability principle: 'Human users have final responsibility for all decisions and outcomes resulting from AI use', so users own what AI helps produce, P29.
units.fit_note: Responsibility for decisions and outcomes, framed for all users, not student submissions specifically.

units.passage: Users are responsible for any published content that incorporates AI-generated material.
units.why: 'Users are responsible for any published content that incorporates AI-generated material' makes users own what they publish, so P29.

units.passage: You are ultimately responsible for the quality and content of the information you submit.
units.why: 'You are ultimately responsible for the quality and content' of submissions makes students own what they submit: P29.

units.passage: I expect all work students submit for this course to be their own.
units.why: "I expect all work students submit for this course to be their own" requires students own their submissions, P29.

units.passage: The work submitted by students in this course will be generated by themselves.
units.why: Submitted work 'will be generated by themselves' requires students' own authorship (P29).

units.passage: All members of the University community must maintain respect for the intellectual efforts of others and be honest in their own work, words and ideas
units.why: "All members of the University community must ... be honest in their own work, words and ideas" binds everyone to honest authorship of their own work, which is P29.

units.passage: In instances where the use of GAI is permitted, the student will: a.) accept responsibility as owner of their work submitted and therefore accept responsibility for the validity of the content
units.why: Where GAI is permitted the student will "accept responsibility as owner of their work submitted", including the validity of content, so P29 (accountability for what is submitted).

units.passage: Tufts faculty, staff, and students are responsible and accountable for content and decisions they create using AI.
units.why: Faculty, staff and students are "responsible and accountable for content and decisions they create using AI"; ownership of what one produces is P29.

units.passage: This applies equally to students completing assignments, faculty developing course materials or evaluating student work, staff performing administrative tasks, and those providing clinical care.
units.why: Extends the accountability duty to every role ("applies equally to students ... faculty ... staff"). It is a scope statement for the accountability principle, coded P29 since it says everyone owns what they produce with AI.
units.fit_note: Scope statement that the accountability duty covers every role (students, faculty, staff, clinicians), not only students' ownership of submissions.

units.passage: All submitted work must be entirely your own.
units.why: "All submitted work must be entirely your own" requires students to own what they submit, P29.

units.passage: Any writing, media, or other submissions not explicitly identified as AI-generated will be assumed as original to the student(s).
units.why: Anything "not explicitly identified as AI-generated will be assumed as original", so unmarked work is the student's own claim, P29.

units.passage: However, all submitted work must reflect your own understanding and effort.
units.why: Requires submitted work to 'reflect your own understanding and effort': ownership (P29). Reconciled codes: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, type P29, unit stance neutral.

units.passage: You are the sole author and intellectual owner of your work, and you are therefore fully responsible for any AI-generated content you incorporate into assignments, research, or publications
units.why: 'sole author and intellectual owner ... fully responsible for any AI-generated content you incorporate' makes students own what they submit, P29.

units.passage: Your grade rests on the accuracy of your submission, not the tool's. You are solely responsible for fact-checking and critically evaluating all AI-generated output before submitting it — and generative tools cannot see the paywalled scholarship your assignment likely depends on.
units.why: 'Your grade rests on the accuracy of your submission, not the tool's' puts accountability for outputs on the student, P29.

units.passage: You will be responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content you submit regardless of whether it originally came from you or an AI model.
units.why: 'You will be responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content you submit' makes the student responsible for submitted work (P29).

units.passage: Include the prompts you used, and answer this question: Who is the author of this work? Then explain your answer.
units.policy: Students answer the question 'Who is the author of this work?' and explain their answer.
units.why: 'Who is the author of this work? Then explain your answer.' makes students reason about authorship, nearest P29 (own what you submit) but it is a required explanation.
units.fit_note: Authorship is raised as a required question and explanation, not as a plain ownership rule.

units.passage: you must document and attribute all AI contributions to your coursework and take full responsibility for the contributions including the accuracy of the information and reliability of sources.
units.why: "take full responsibility for the contributions including the accuracy of the information and reliability of sources" makes students own what they submit, P29.

units.passage: Regardless of what you use to compose, you are responsible for what you turn in.
units.why: "Regardless of what you use to compose, you are responsible for what you turn in", P29.

units.passage: This will inevitably improve over time, but the human operator is ultimately responsible for the code and its operation.
units.why: "the human operator is ultimately responsible for the code and its operation" makes the user own AI-assisted code, P29, must.

units.passage: Be aware that students are responsible for any errors or information that is misrepresented or inaccurate (i.e. hallucinations) that generative AI tools produce when submitting work that includes AI-generated material
units.policy: Students are responsible for any errors or inaccurate information (hallucinations) that generative AI tools produce when they submit work that includes AI-generated material.
units.why: "students are responsible for any errors or information that is misrepresented or inaccurate (i.e. hallucinations)" makes students own what AI contributes to submitted work. P29 (own what you submit) is chosen over P31 because the passage assigns responsibility rather than telling students to verify.

units.passage: the responsibility for the work, learning, validity, authenticity, and accuracy always lies with the human researcher
units.policy: The responsibility for the work, learning, validity, authenticity, and accuracy always lies with the human researcher.
units.why: The policy says 'the responsibility for the work, learning, validity, authenticity, and accuracy always lies with the human researcher', putting ownership on the human; P29.

units.passage: The final responsibility for the quality, accuracy, and academic integrity of a research project, a research presentation or manuscript, or creative work produced with the assistance of AI lies with the student
units.policy: The final responsibility for the quality, accuracy, and academic integrity of a research project, presentation, manuscript or creative work produced with AI assistance lies with the student.
units.why: 'final responsibility for the quality, accuracy, and academic integrity ... lies with the student' - students own the work, P29.

units.passage: Individuals using AI technologies are accountable for their actions and decisions facilitated by AI systems.
units.why: Users stay accountable for decisions facilitated by AI. Closest is P29 (students own what they submit), applied to all users.
units.fit_note: Coder A: Applies to all users' actions and decisions, not specifically to submitted student work. | Coder B: Applies to all individuals using AI, not specifically to submitted student work.

units.passage: You use AI to help brainstorm, build outlines, search for tools, explain concepts, and generate ideas, but the actual content you submit is your own
units.why: 'the actual content you submit is your own' limits Level 2 so AI cannot be the author of what is submitted; the student owns the submission (P29).

units.passage: The key responsibility is the human review of everything AI produces, ensuring accuracy, and making sure the final product reflects your own judgment and understanding.
units.why: Level 4 'key responsibility is the human review of everything AI produces' and the product must reflect the student's judgment; P29 chosen over P31 since it centers on the final product reflecting own judgment.

units.passage: You are accountable for your work product, whether AI helped create it or not.
units.why: A guiding principle that places responsibility on the user: 'You are accountable for your work product, whether AI helped create it or not.' P29 (own what you submit) fits; the audience is employees but the rule is the same.

units.passage: Where attribution is expected, provide it, regardless of whether AI assisted in the creation.
units.why: Attribution duties stay the same whether or not AI helped ("regardless of whether AI assisted"), so the user owns attribution: P29; P24 would imply an AI disclosure that is not what is said.

units.passage: Students will be responsible for the content and quality of their assignment submissions, which are expected to meet the assignment criteria and demonstrate students’ own ideas, interpretation, and effort.
units.why: 'Students will be responsible for the content and quality of their assignment submissions': ownership of submitted work, P29.

units.passage: You are the author of content that you produce with AI and responsible for its accuracy, impact, and compliance with relevant laws and policies.
units.policy: The user is the author of content produced with AI and is responsible for its accuracy, impact, and compliance with relevant laws and policies.
units.why: "You are the author of content that you produce with AI and responsible for its accuracy" makes the user own and answer for the output, matching P29; the accuracy duty touches P31 but ownership is the main claim.

units.passage: Faculty and students are the authors of content generated by AI and are responsible for that content as they are with content that they author.
units.policy: Faculty and students are the authors of content generated by AI and are responsible for that content as they are with content that they author.
units.why: "Faculty and students are the authors of content generated by AI and are responsible for that content" repeats ownership for both groups as a principle bullet; P29, kept separate because it is the principles list and names faculty too.

units.passage: How will I ensure my students understand their responsibility for AI-generated content?
units.why: "How will I ensure my students understand their responsibility for AI-generated content?" asks the instructor to make students accountable for AI output; P29.

units.passage: Students may not claim as their own work any portion of academic work that was not created by the student.
units.why: 'Students may not claim as their own work any portion of academic work that was not created by the student' is a general ownership rule that the Code applies to AI. P29 fits because it requires submitted work to be the student's own.

units.passage: “Students may not claim as their own work any portion of academic work that was not completed by the student.”
units.why: 'Students may not claim as their own work any portion of academic work that was not completed by the student' restates the Code's rule on this page. P29 fits.

units.passage: The writing should belong to you, and it should remain your own work.
units.why: 'The writing should belong to you, and it should remain your own work' is an ownership rule. P29 fits.

units.passage: [This course] assumes that all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves, working individually or in groups.
units.why: 'assumes that all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves' is an ownership rule for the course. P29 fits.

units.passage: All students, faculty, and staff are responsible for any content published, shared, or otherwise developed that includes any AI-generated material
units.why: "All students, faculty, and staff are responsible for any content published... that includes any AI-generated material" makes users own what they publish, P29.

units.passage: Employees shall only use AI tools that meet organizational security standards, not input any personally identifiable or confidential information, and fact check AI-generated content before using it in official University documents as they remain accountable for any work products even if AI was used to assist in their creation.
units.why: Employees "remain accountable for any work products even if AI was used to assist"; ownership of output, P29.

units.passage: To uphold academic integrity, students must submit work that they have completed themselves in accordance with the guidelines for the course and instructions for the assignment.
units.why: "students must submit work that they have completed themselves in accordance with the guidelines for the course"; work must be the student's own, P29.

units.passage: If questions arise about the authorship of student-submitted work, it is the student’s responsibility to authenticate authorship.
units.why: "it is the student’s responsibility to authenticate authorship" when authorship is questioned; students own their work, P29.
units.fit_note: Also sets who bears the burden of proving authorship in a dispute.

units.passage: Remind your students that they are ultimately responsible for the work they submit.
units.why: "Remind your students that they are ultimately responsible for the work they submit." Students own what they submit, so P29, with the instructor as actor.

units.passage: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish.
units.why: "You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish" makes users answerable for AI-assisted output, so P29.

units.passage: All work must represent your own independent effort and original thinking.
units.why: Template 2: 'All work must represent your own independent effort and original thinking', a statement that submitted work is the student's own (P29).

units.passage: You are ultimately responsible and accountable for your use of GenAI and all outcomes derived from it
units.why: 'You are ultimately responsible and accountable for your use of GenAI and all outcomes' makes users own what results from AI, P29.
units.fit_note: Applies to all uses and outcomes, not only submitted work.

units.passage: For these reasons, all work submitted for this course must be your own
units.why: 'all work submitted for this course must be your own' is the ownership requirement in the no-AI sample, P29.

units.passage: An engineer uses tools responsibly and knows they are accountable for their own work output regardless of their tools.
units.why: 'An engineer uses tools responsibly and knows they are accountable for their own work output regardless of their tools': students own their work, P29.

units.passage: Students are solely responsible for their final product, including AI - generated content, as if they had produced the materials themselves
units.why: 'Students are solely responsible for their final product, including AI-generated content, as if they had produced the materials themselves' makes students own what they submit, P29.

units.passage: Affirm that the submitted work is their own
units.why: 'Affirm that the submitted work is their own' asks students to attest ownership of submissions, P29.
units.fit_note: Delivered as an attestation step the instructor arranges.

units.passage: Use honor statements at the start of exams or submissions
units.why: 'Use honor statements at the start of exams or submissions' adds an honor pledge to submissions, P29 (students own what they submit).
units.fit_note: It is an attestation device (honor statement) rather than only a statement of ownership.

units.passage: “Students are responsible for the honest completion and representation of their work, for the appropriate citation of sources, and for respect of others’ academic endeavors.”
units.why: The quote from UWS Chapter 14 says students are responsible for honest completion and representation of work and appropriate citation; this is ownership of submitted work (P29).

units.passage: According to section UWS 14.03(2): “Examples of academic misconduct include, but are not limited to: cheating on an examination; collaborating with others in work to be presented, contrary to the stated rules of the course; submitting a paper or assignment as one’s own work when a part or all of the paper or assignment is the work of another; submitting a paper or assignment that contains ideas or research of others without appropriately identifying the sources of those ideas; stealing examinations or course materials; submitting, if contrary to the rules of a course, work previously presented in another course; tampering with the laboratory experiment or computer program of another student; knowingly and intentionally assisting another student in any of the above, including assistance in an arrangement whereby any work, classroom performance, examination or other activity is submitted or performed by a person other than the student under whose name the work is submitted or performed.”
units.why: Quoting UWS 14.03(2): "submitting a paper or assignment as one’s own work when a part or all of the paper or assignment is the work of another" is misconduct; ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.fit_note: Defines misconduct (P36 aspect); P29 chosen because the passage is about submitting others' work as one's own.
